claims.text: A Co-Ni-Fe multi-principal-element binder produces finer WC grains than a conventional Co binder.
Adding Nb or Ta to the WC-Co-Ni-Fe binder will form a secondary BCC phase.
The proposed binder and refractory addition will provide ultra-high hardness, high density, and better high-temperature oxidation resistance than conventional WC-Co.
A carbon content of 5.46 wt% prevents eta-phase formation in the proposed carbide.
Low-pressure sintering at 1450 °C under 5.0 MPa argon is an established processing condition for ultrafine WC-10CoNiFe.
The MPE binder suppresses WC dissolution-precipitation during sintering and thereby produces a fine-grained microstructure.
Rapid cooling can lock in the proposed fine-grained, dual-phase structure.
The relevant investigated processing window is 1410–1500 °C, 5.44–5.50 wt% carbon, and 5.0 MPa argon.
WC-10CoNiFe can achieve an average WC grain size of approximately 0.261 µm under its optimal reported conditions.
The Co-Ni-Fe binder reduces WC solubility in the liquid phase during sintering.
A Nb- or Ta-containing secondary phase acts as a barrier to WC grain coarsening.
The refractory addition forms a protective oxide scale that improves oxidation resistance.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the binder solid solution against high-temperature phase separation.
The Nb-modified material will exceed 1765 HV and 3000 MPa flexural strength.
The proposed material will have significantly better oxidation resistance than WC-Co at 1000–1500 °C.
The proposed material will reach more than 95% theoretical density because grain growth and pore formation are suppressed.
Optimal WC-10Co has 3598 MPa flexural strength, 1853 HV hardness, and a 0.294 µm grain size, whereas optimal WC-10CoNiFe has 2999 MPa strength, 1765 HV hardness, and a 0.261 µm grain size.
Conventional WC-Co has lower oxidation resistance than WC-10CoNiFe.
Carbon must remain within 5.44–5.50 wt% to avoid eta phase or graphite, and temperatures above 1500 °C cause grain coarsening that negates refinement.
Exceeding the refractory element's solubility limit will create brittle secondary phases that reduce toughness.

contradictions.description: The proposed route is low-pressure argon sintering after uniaxial pressing, but the falsification experiment switches to spark plasma sintering. This processing change may alter densification, phase formation, and grain growth, so it does not directly test the stated route.
